[NEW in run 002] docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-03/topic-04.mdx line 118 states that 'Furlich (2016) surveyed 77 undergraduates at one United States university', and the Further reading entry at lines 255-256 repeats 'Note the setting: 77 undergraduates at one United States university'. The bound excerpt specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/furlich2016.md, whose provenance is declared as the verbatim abstract, states in its own scope note: 'The abstract does NOT state the sample size. Unit 3 prose cites "N=77"; that figure is not confirmed by this excerpt and needs the full text or the methods section to verify.' The abstract likewise says only 'a small liberal arts university' and names no country, so 'United States' is a reasonable inference from the journal and institution type but is not read in the source. The direction of Furlich's result - verbal immediacy significant, non-verbal not - IS verbatim-supported and is not in question. This is precisely the distinction the unit itself teaches in the same topic, which makes an unverified specific figure a poor thing to leave standing. REPAIR: bind the methods passage that gives N, or drop the specific figure and the country and keep 'one small liberal arts university', which the abstract does support verbatim.
